stable_tendencies: TARGET_A07 often meets practical expectations by following detailed instructions or joining requested tasks rather than proposing an alternative. [D1-Q1-C01]
TARGET_A07 is portrayed as applying common-sense and social-context judgments in unusual situations. [D1-Q3-C02]
TARGET_A07 works to preserve cohesion and continuing closeness within a friend group. [D2-Q1-C02]
motives_and_goals: Observers interpret TARGET_A07 as repeatedly seeking dependable love and reassurance associated with affection perceived as missing from an early maternal relationship. [D2-Q1-C01]
TARGET_A07 appears motivated to maintain close relationships and may fear that a partner's increased independence could lead to abandonment. [D2-Q2-C01; D4-Q3-C01]
TARGET_A07 seeks partner approval through giving, affection, and efforts at self-improvement, apparently using acceptance as confirmation of worth. [D6-Q3-C02; D7-Q2-C02]
TARGET_A07 aims to sustain cohesion and ongoing access to valued friends. [D2-Q1-C02]
value_priorities: TARGET_A07 prioritizes loyalty and felt obligation to a close associate over taking an independent stand, within the documented close-relationship context. [D3-Q1-C01]
TARGET_A07 places substantial value on relational continuity, belonging, and being needed. [D2-Q1-C02; D4-Q3-C01]
In recovery from family-related distress, TARGET_A07 appears to value freedom from resentment and from dependence on an unchanging person's approval. [D5-Q3-C01]
cognitive_appraisal_model: TARGET_A07 is portrayed as reading unusual situations through everyday social norms and contextual common sense. [D1-Q3-C02]
TARGET_A07 may interpret criticism or rejection through doubts about personal adequacy, sometimes contributing to self-undermining behavior. [D4-Q2-C01]
TARGET_A07 may appraise acceptance as conditional on performance, improvement, or evaluation and consequently question secure lovability. [D4-Q3-C02; D7-Q1-C02]
In close relationships, TARGET_A07 may construe another person's growth as a threat to mutual dependence and relationship security. [D2-Q2-C01; D4-Q3-C01]
affective_dynamics: Repeated criticism, bullying, humiliation, or invasive mistreatment can produce pronounced distress and sometimes intense anger in TARGET_A07. [D5-Q1-C01]
Family-related recovery is portrayed as occurring through accepting that the other person will not change, forgiving, and releasing the pursuit of approval. [D5-Q3-C01]
Relational insecurity appears emotionally salient when TARGET_A07 anticipates becoming unnecessary or being left behind. [D4-Q3-C01]
interpersonal_patterns: TARGET_A07 commonly accommodates a demanding close associate, including complying with demands and helping with unwanted tasks. [D1-Q1-C01; D6-Q2-C04]
TARGET_A07 acts as a cohesion-maintaining and protective presence within a friend group. [D2-Q1-C02]
TARGET_A07's willingness to confront others varies with anticipated social cost: challenge is more likely when acceptance is less at risk. [D4-Q2-C04]
When a demanding close associate threatens another desired connection, TARGET_A07 may shift from accommodation to hostility. [D6-Q2-C04]
Partner conflict may cycle through affection, resentment, blame, and reconciliation without deep resolution of underlying issues. [D6-Q2-C05]
Relationships with an emotionally authoritative parent and a closest friend are portrayed as especially influential in TARGET_A07's interpersonal development. [D7-Q1-C03]
self_narrative_themes: Observers frame painful maternal treatment during childhood as formative to TARGET_A07's later struggles involving love, validation, and agency. [D7-Q1-C01]
TARGET_A07's growth narrative includes recognizing that an emotionally authoritative person will not change and becoming less governed by that person's approval. [D5-Q3-C01]
TARGET_A07 appears to connect being accepted by a partner with having improved enough to be worthy. [D7-Q2-C02]
TARGET_A07 is portrayed as capable of romantic success despite a shy or conventionally unappealing self-presentation. [D7-Q2-C03]
situation_behavior_signatures: When given detailed practical expectations by a close other, TARGET_A07 tends to comply or assist rather than refuse. [D1-Q1-C01]
When social situations become unusual, TARGET_A07 tends to supply a comparatively grounded, context-sensitive appraisal. [D1-Q3-C02]
When confrontation risks losing highly desired affection, TARGET_A07 is more likely to tolerate objectionable conduct; lower-cost confrontation is more feasible. [D4-Q2-C04]
When another person's conduct threatens access to a valued connection, TARGET_A07 may become less accommodating and more hostile. [D6-Q2-C04]
When subjected to repeated humiliation or invasive provocation, TARGET_A07 may move from distress toward intense anger. [D5-Q1-C01]
contradictions_boundary_conditions: TARGET_A07's accommodation is not universal: it can reverse when compliance threatens another valued relationship or social opportunity. [D6-Q2-C04]
Context-sensitive social judgment coexists with a tendency to process rejection through doubts about personal adequacy. [D1-Q3-C02; D4-Q2-C01]
TARGET_A07 seeks improvement and approval but is also described as behaving in ways that undermine desired outcomes. [D7-Q3-C01]

Relationship preservation is emphasized in close partnerships, whereas recovery from family distress is associated with relinquishing approval from someone judged unlikely to change. [D4-Q3-C01; D5-Q3-C01]
unknown_contested: A generalized characterization of TARGET_A07 as consistently insecure or underconfident is disputed by counterevidence, although adequacy doubts are supported in criticism and relationship contexts. [D1-Q3-C01; D8-Q1-C04]
The breadth of TARGET_A07's self-sacrificing accommodation is disputed; evidence supports several helping episodes but also situational refusal or hostility. [D3-Q2-C01; D3-Q2-C02]
It is unresolved whether TARGET_A07 maintains relationships primarily from genuine loyalty or instrumentally to preserve intimacy and access. [D3-Q2-C02]

Claims that TARGET_A07 selects companions to appear superior, avoids unfavorable comparisons, or maintains a dominant self-image remain weak or contested motive attributions. [D2-Q2-C02; D6-Q1-C03; D7-Q2-C01]
Whether TARGET_A07 broadly blames past mistreatment for present failures rather than exercising agency is contested or weakly supported. [D4-Q2-C02; D4-Q3-C03]

Resistance to a partner's independence, enabling of mutual dependence, and preservation of hurtful relationship patterns remain partly inferential and unevenly supported. [D2-Q1-C03; D3-Q3-C02; D6-Q3-C03]
Claims that TARGET_A07 avoids honest breakup explanations or persists after an explicit refusal are based on limited evidence. [D2-Q2-C04; D6-Q2-C03]
Fearful submission to physically intimidating people and avoidance of public humiliation are supported only by a limited confrontation account. [D2-Q2-C03; D6-Q1-C04; D8-Q1-C03]
Difficulty receiving affection as fully as TARGET_A07 gives it is repeatedly described but derives from one weak observer account. [D5-Q1-C02; D5-Q2-C01; D5-Q3-C04; D6-Q2-C02]
A general tendency toward extreme anger is disputed; stronger evidence limits anger escalation to repeated criticism, humiliation, or invasive provocation. [D8-Q1-C01; D5-Q1-C01]
Sarcasm appears recurrent, but whether it is cutting or comparatively mild is disputed. [D8-Q3-C01]
Self-deprecating humor about insecurity, emotionally disruptive remarks, and conspicuous eyebrow-based expression have limited support. [D8-Q3-C02; D8-Q3-C03; D8-Q3-C05]
Appearance-related anxiety, concealment through clothing, and a specific privacy boundary involving TARGET_A07's feet are speculative and contested. [D3-Q3-C03; D5-Q1-C04; D5-Q2-C03]
Whether TARGET_A07 can reliably read broader social cues is contested despite supported portrayals of context-sensitive common sense. [D6-Q1-C01; D8-Q3-C04; D1-Q3-C02]
A firm boundary around something personally earned appears in one episode but conflicts with broader descriptions of infrequent self-assertion. [D3-Q3-C01]
